stem: Amiodarone is used to treat and prevent which cardiac rhythm problems?

options.label: A
options.misconception: None — amiodarone treats and prevents certain types of ventricular arrhythmias.
options.explanation: MedlinePlus lists amiodarone, an antiarrhythmic, to treat and prevent certain types of ventricular arrhythmias.

options.label: B
options.text: Certain nonshockable arrest rhythms, such as asystole
options.misconception: Assumes the arrest antiarrhythmic helps every cardiac arrest rhythm, including nonshockable ones.
options.explanation: Asystole and PEA are nonshockable arrests managed with CPR and epinephrine; amiodarone is used in arrest only for VF or pulseless VT.

options.label: C
options.text: Certain bradyarrhythmias, such as sick sinus syndrome
options.misconception: Treats any rhythm disorder as an amiodarone indication, ignoring its rate-slowing effect.
options.explanation: Sick sinus syndrome and symptomatic bradycardia need atropine or pacing; amiodarone slows the sinus rate and would worsen them.

options.label: D
options.text: Certain types of heart block, such as Mobitz II
options.misconception: Forgets that amiodarone depresses AV nodal conduction, so it cannot treat heart block.
options.explanation: High-grade AV block such as Mobitz II needs pacing; amiodarone slows AV nodal conduction and can precipitate or worsen block.

options.label: E
options.text: Torsades de pointes from drug-induced long QT
options.misconception: Forgets that amiodarone prolongs the QT interval, so it is not the treatment for torsades.
options.explanation: Torsades is treated with IV magnesium and removal of QT-prolonging drugs; amiodarone itself prolongs the QT interval.

context: Learning objective: Amiodarone is an antiarrhythmic used to treat and prevent certain types of ventricular arrhythmias.
